reviews.title: Keep improving
reviews.text:
Overall, Jobber is a great platform, but there are several areas that definitely need improvement, particularly with the mobile app, AI Receptionist, client records, and third-party integrations. As a business owner who relies on Jobber daily, these are practical improvements that would make a significant difference in efficiency.

1. Technician Time Tracking

Business owners should be able to view technicians’ time entries and hours worked on individual jobs directly from the mobile app. This information should be readily accessible without having to switch to the desktop version.

2. AI Receptionist Call History

Every incoming call should have a clearly displayed date and timestamp. Phone numbers should also be clickable, allowing us to return calls directly from the AI Receptionist’s call history.

Currently, unless a caller submits an actual request that becomes associated with a client profile, we have to manually copy and paste the phone number to return the call. This is an unnecessary inconvenience that should be easy to correct.

3. Better Integration Between Pages

There needs to be more seamless navigation between AI Receptionist conversations, call history, client profiles, requests, and jobs. Information should be interconnected without requiring users to constantly switch between screens or manually transfer details.

4. Native Mobile Text Messaging

There should be an option to open a customer’s phone number in the device’s native text messaging app rather than being limited to messaging within Jobber.

Many customers initially contact us through regular text messages. Having the flexibility to communicate through our phone’s messaging app, while ideally maintaining a connection to their Jobber client profile, would be extremely valuable.

5. Centralized Client Attachments and Photos

All attachments, including photos and documents uploaded to individual jobs, should automatically populate in a centralized attachment section within the client’s main profile.

Currently, having to open individual jobs to locate previously uploaded photos or documents is unnecessarily time-consuming, especially when a customer has a long service history.

There should be one consolidated list or gallery showing every attachment associated with that customer, regardless of which job it was originally uploaded to. Ideally, each attachment would also link back to its original job for reference.

6. Better Two-Way Integration With CompanyCam

The CompanyCam integration is a great example of a feature that has potential but needs better connectivity.

I appreciate that Jobber can automatically create a corresponding project in CompanyCam. However, there should also be a direct link within the Jobber client or job profile that opens the associated CompanyCam project, and vice versa.

If the integration already connects the two platforms and creates the corresponding project, there should be no reason we can’t navigate directly between them. This would eliminate unnecessary searching and make the integration significantly more useful.

Overall Feedback

These aren’t extravagant feature requests. They’re basic workflow improvements that would save contractors and business owners considerable time throughout the day.

Jobber continues to introduce new features, particularly AI-powered tools, but I believe greater attention needs to be given to improving the functionality, navigation, and integration of the features already available.

A truly efficient platform should make information accessible from wherever you’re working, whether that’s a client’s profile, an individual job, the AI Receptionist, or an integrated application like CompanyCam.

I would really like to see these improvements prioritized and implemented sooner rather than later. Jobber is already a valuable business management tool, but addressing these everyday frustrations would make it substantially better for the contractors who depend on it.

reviews.title: Poor excuse for a time card
reviews.text:
one of the two worst workplace solutions and definitely the worst digital punch card I’ve ever had the displeasure of using both as a laborer and an owner. You are better off grabbing a notepad, a pencil, and a manilla folder like it’s still 2003, than you are falling for jobbers marketing. 

You are better off giving your guys a timesheet every week, and having them log their hours and job name the old fashioned way. Genuinely nothing this thing does justifies the absurd price, poor interface, workplace confusion, and absolutely asinine job setup. The AI features are wholly unnecessary, add zero actual convenience to day to day use of the app and unironically they are the only ones that will consistently work. 
Doesn’t matter though, your guys can’t clock in unless the connection is rock solid. guys can’t see the job you’ve assigned them to half the time either unless you mess around with it on a computer while they’re in the app so  despite paying for a solution you’ll be calling and texting your employees in the morning like you always have anyway. 



My guys aren’t clocking out for lunch because your app wont let them clock in afterwards, so it looks like they’re working through every lunch. Any idea how bad that looks? 

The ability to clock in and out while offline and the app automatically sending it out when you reconnect is something plenty of existing timecard apps have already figured out and built in. The fact that this one doesn’t makes whatever vibe coded nonsense you threw together on top of the poor time clock (seriously? one job.) suck more. It also gets people who just need to clock in and out with this pile’ in trouble with their boss,  who, thanks to Jobbers’™️©️®️ awful, misleading, marketing, think a glorified punch clock where your laborers can write down what their job of moving and gophering was that day can go any sort of way towards replacing a proper invoice and job summary. 

Less than useless.

Their “support team” are forced to make it up as they go, no one with real accountability AND authority/ability to help.

My only stipulation was it did not handle recurring billing very well, this was somewhat misrepresented to me when I was purchasing the software, but I figured it was a simple miscommunication. I explained to the sales rep that we are in Alarm Company and need to handle recurring billing and she told me Jobber could handle that. It turns out the recurring billing wants to be tied to a job every time. I’m sure that’s fine if you’re mowing lawns. But it doesn’t make much sense for you to receive a job completion Email after your alarm bill has been charged to your credit card. Their solution for this? Disable job completion emails. Well now I’m missing a major feature of the platform because these customers still have other types of jobs. I said no problem, help me do a payment data export through stripe (which jobber uses for payment processing) that way I could use a different tool only to handle my recurring billing. I was going to stay with jobber for everything else. They refused. They offered to make a feature suggestion. That is completely unacceptable. They’re holding my customers payment data hostage, and support is not replying when I asked them if I am the merchant of record or if they are the merchant of record.  If I have to recollect all my customers payment data I’m switching away from jobber entirely. 

Do yourself a favor and do not use this app, for any business that builds RMR, the easiest way to attrition is having to ask customers to update their payment method, then they suddenly remember they don’t want the service anymore. So thank you Jobber for a great reminder why you should vet all your sass apps and never EVER use a platform that does not allow you to bring your own payment processor.

I’ve been using the free trial for a week and I’ve liked it so far. I will be getting the Connect plan for my business. I really like the automatic messages to remind clients of their appointments as well as follow ups after the job to get reviews. I’ve even had customers comment on how they like my new system. 

It’s been a learning curve trying to get used to everything. It’s presented as an easy dashboard and it looks simple but when you start adding jobs to the calendar and making some jobs recurring it does get a little confusing. 

There are some things I wish were easier. When you click on your jobs in the calendar it will show you the work that needs to be done, but it doesn’t show you how much money the job is for. I still haven’t figured out how to see that. 

When you have a recurring job and you need to cancel the entire thing you can’t just delete the job from the calendar, you have to go to the job number and delete them from there. You should be able to delete all of the recurring jobs from the calendar instead of making it a hide and seek game trying to figure out how to remove them all.

On the mobile app, when you go to add a job, it doesn’t allow you to add in a business’s name. Why in the world is that not an option? It seems like a glaring oversight on Jobber’s part. If you want to add a new job and it’s a business they make you go to “existing customer” first and then add a new client and then go all the way back to the calendar to add the job. It doesn’t make sense, just add a company name line as optional to the add job form. 

The last thing I don’t love is on the mobile app it’s really difficult to see your whole calendar for the month. They only allow you to see one day at a time. At least let us see a week at a time. It would make it so much easier to know what’s available to put a customer in. Instead I’ve been pulling up the website on my browser to see my calendar on jobber. 

All in all I’ve had a good experience, and I think it’s going to help revolutionize my business. There are some annoying things they should fix to streamline the system more, especially on the app, but I’m still planning on using it.

They need to dedicate more resources to development to actually finish ANY of the modules they’ve built. 

It’s all half or 3/4 baked.

No switching job titles.   Almost every Hvac company out there is sending estimates as multiple options, at least two, and Jobber forces you to upgrade to the “Grow” plan to get packages. The top tier plan.  This is a one time payment of $2,988 right out the gate, or $349mo.   Packages should be available on the “Connect plan”, with the ability to add/select items and pictures on the grow plan for an upgrade to those who want that.  Packages is a middle tier item. Need to make a more attractive monthly payment also, not everyone can just drop $3k to get a decent price.  Jobber was more attractive at $119mo & $199mo. Now it’s $169 and $349mo  I don’t want to know that my price is going up after 12 months either. No promo stuff.  Your already making thousands off the credit card processing fees, want to gouge me with an increasing subscription service too?  In a day with rising subscription costs, the last thing we want is more subscriptions.  Make the Connect plan more appealing, and lock in the rates. 

Our current software does all of these things at a fraction of the cost, so we are not seeing the value here, for Hvac companies at least should probably look elsewhere.

reviews.title: I came back to Jobber after leaving to try Bookingkoala
reviews.text:
I had left Jobber for bookingkoala because I was interested in some things that BK does well and Jobber is missing. I came back bc BK is so challenging to learn. If the Dev Tm can address some of these Jobber will be a better system, because it will combine some strengths of BK with the strengths of Jobber

1. An app for admin that looks like the website. I realize this is a tall task and it’s actually not my number 1 suggestion, I just put it in first. Keep reading. 
2. Timesheets currently do not sync with QB for Contractors. I use 1099 contractors and they record their time in Jobber. In QB they are not employees, they are contractors, so their hours don’t sync and I have to manually translate.
3. Notifications for Providers are lacking. One huge advantage of BK is notifications to providers are automatic. In Jobber, when I create a new job and assign a provider, I should not have to select “send notification email to provider” this is obvious that it should be preselected because There is no such thing as spam when automating business operations. Furthermore, i should be able to have the system automatically send email reminders to providers xxx days/hours in advance of the job.
4. Photos in the notes section. The notes section is nice but the most important thing is easily sharing this with clients. When creating an invoice, I should have the option to share notes with client so they can see the photos. This needs to be easier to learn and see. I have tons of jobs with photos in the notes and I haven’t ignited out how to easily share with clients
5. Jobber Payments. BK has the big advantage here because the admin does not have to leave BK to pay the provider. You simply assign a price to pay the provider and click pay. The funds are routed automatically through Stripe. Stripe Payments is literally free, so cost is way lower.
6. Cost. This is Jobbers #1 issue in my opinion. Using Jobber costs a relative fortune. For many of us, you need Jobber which is already expensive, you need quickbooks, and you need quickbooks payments. This is roughly $400 per month depending on team size. You can get the same production out of BK and Stripe for about $100 per month. I switched back bc Jobber is simply easier in some aspects, but because of the price, I will always be searching for a better value.

reviews.title: Jobber website better than the app
reviews.text:
I really like Jobber, but as far as the iPhone app goes, I can’t give it more than three stars. The reason being, the most important thing I use the app for is to be able to take phone calls on the go, do scheduling, etc. I wish it had a better calendar view, I don’t like that you pretty much have to manually click on every date to see when there are availabilities. I also wish it had a notes section. I find myself writing my notes from phone calls out on paper, then adding them to jobber later or when I get home, which kind of defeats the purpose of having an app. Please make the app geared toward management as well!

Update: I’ve lowered my review to two stars after months of using this. It has potential, but it is not user friendly and is really making my job harder. The guys can’t figure out how to use it in the field even though we’ve showed them over and over again, and it’s next to impossible to accomplish anything as a manager for billing in the app. And if I want to schedule a visit for an existing job, why can’t I do it from the calendar? Why do I have to click on ten different things just to accomplish one task? This app needs streamlined and simplified. It also needs the option to do progress invoicing. Not a “deposit”, but actual progress invoicing for when each draw is completed. I will be looking for a different alternative for my scheduling needs.

reviews.title: App crashed in the middle of writing a quote
reviews.text:
Overall good, but can get WAY better

The app crashed while I was in the middle of writing a extensive quote. The quote didn’t get saved and I worked about 10 minutes on creating it before it just crashed. Super inconvenient. I’m using an iPhone 13 pro with the latest OS and the latest app And OS updates automatically installed. 

Also, massive feature requests:
1. Make it so that you can enter timesheets post work. You should be able to record time worked on a project at any time, not just clock in and clock out. Ridiculous that this feature doesnt exist on mobile. 
2. Add service items to your timesheets, just like Tsheets.
3. Be able to attach photos to timesheets
4. Add a “work notes “section to quote line items. This would be way better than one note section for the entire quote. 
5. Add formatting options to line items. Markdown is easy enough and can be easily  and quickly implemented.

Jobber is really nice to work with, really well laid out, and is almost there, just needs some finishing touches. For the cost these features should be there.
